spec_match.rationale: Concepts demonstrate the author-intent layer of w3c/aria PR #1805 (open and unmerged, so proposed rather than normative text): article cards and treeitems — both outside Chromium's preventedOnRoles list in aria_properties.json5 — reference real, named, keyboard-navigable buttons via IDREF lists. They satisfy the proposal's author requirements: accessible names, click-event activation rather than modality-specific handlers, and direct keyboard navigation. Parent review also made the ARIA tree itself keyboard-operable with a named tree, roving tabindex, ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End navigation, and visible treeitem focus. New probes report the exact DOM-level support: content attribute (always present) vs element.ariaActionsElements reflection (RuntimeEnabled=AriaActions) vs unverifiable AT behavior, without conflating them.

interactive.rationale: Real action buttons everywhere (click logging works regardless of browser support), plus the honest DOM-level probe on both concepts. The demo does not fake accessibility-tree exposure or AT activation.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index and concept ledes no longer assert AT/screen-reader exposure as fact: they separate author intent (attribute present), browser DOM reflection (ariaActionsElements — probed live), and AT behavior (explicitly out of scope for a headless page). Availability is stated exactly: v151 listing Enabled by default on Win/Mac/Linux desktop; detail 'In development' (updated 2026-07-01); not ChromeOS/Android per the launch intent in runtime_enabled_features.json5; ARIA change is the unmerged PR #1805.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers the absent-reflection path (this Chrome 150: probe reports undefined with the exact availability context), the wrong-name trap (ariaActions vs ariaActionsElements, encoded in the suite), and headless/no-AT limits stated on-page. role=article/treeitem hosts verified valid (not in Chromium's preventedOnRoles: caption/code/definition/deletion/emphasis/generic/insertion/mark/paragraph/strong/subscript/suggestion/superscript/term/time).

references.rationale: All pages cite chromestatus.com/feature/5161589307867136 and the ARIA PR #1805 (labelled open/unmerged); the root also links the exact Chromium binding and runtime configuration. The critique/suite use aria_relationship_attributes.idl, aria_properties.json5, runtime_enabled_features.json5, and core_enums for recorded vendor signals without reinterpreting them. Exact MDN routes for the aria-actions attribute, Element.ariaActionsElements, and ElementInternals.ariaActionsElements all return 404; current BCD Element, ElementInternals, and global-attributes data contains neither ariaActionsElements nor aria-actions, so no support versions are inferred from MDN/BCD.

conformance.rationale: New immutable root suite (this cycle, 9 assertions — JSON entries and rendered rows must stay aligned): Element and ElementInternals existence, content-attribute roundtrip (explicitly markup-only), ariaActionsElements exposure on Element and the ElementInternals prototype, the wrong-name-absent trap, not-static binding, reflection value shape, and strict referenced-element resolution. Parent tightened the valid-IDREF contract to require exactly the referenced button rather than allowing null/empty results that would hide a broken implementation. No AT is assumed and no activation is automated.

runtime_evidence.rationale: chrome-devtools-mcp on HeadlessChrome/150 (reflection absent, verified): all visible controls exercised at 1280×800 and 390×844 with post-interaction geometry — both probes report content-attribute-present + reflection-undefined with the exact availability text, all action buttons log correctly, tap targets re-measured at 44px after the min-height fix, focus-visible outlines present, zero console errors and zero failed requests.

telemetry_health.rationale: Both concepts emit showcaseTelemetry.assert events for their probe runs (aria-actions-probe-ran / aria-actions-tree-probe-ran with the reflected flag); telemetry POSTs returned 202 during validation.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, button background+color pairs (repo invariant #6), focus-visible outlines added where missing, no static-card pattern; edits were copy/probe/style level and preserve layout.

accessibility.rationale: Native buttons are keyboard-navigable and click-activated as the proposal requires; visible focus and text accessible names are present; probes/logs use role=status/aria-live; tap targets are 44px. Parent review added the missing accessible tree contract: a named role=tree, focusable treeitems with levels and roving tabindex, ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End movement, and visible treeitem focus.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Matrix pass including post-interaction states: all three pages scrollWidth equals viewport at 1280×800 and 390×844 after clicking action buttons (readouts wrap; card grid auto-fits; tree rows flex-wrap).

openQuestions.title: Re-verify reflection and a11y-tree exposure on a Chrome 151+ desktop build
openQuestions.detail: This environment runs HeadlessChrome/150, where ariaActionsElements is undefined. On a 151+ Win/Mac/Linux build (runtime feature AriaActions stable per runtime_enabled_features.json5; not ChromeOS/Android), re-run both probes to verify the reflection resolves referenced elements, and if possible check the accessibility-tree mapping with a real AT — which no headless page can assert. Also track w3c/aria PR #1805 (unmerged as of 2026-07-24) for normative changes and the preventedOnRoles list.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible composite widgets with secondary actions keyboard navigation focus management
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Every interactive element needs keyboard access, visible focus, an accessible name, and adequate target size; announce dynamic state via live regions.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: native buttons throughout (keyboard + click per the PR's author requirements), focus-visible outlines added, tap targets raised to 44px, probes/logs use role=status/aria-live.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: chrome-devtools-mcp measurement after fixes at 1280×800 and 390×844, 2026-07-24

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible form controls buttons target size keyboard operation in interactive demo pages
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Buttons must be keyboard-operable with visible focus and adequate (44px-ish) activation targets.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: min-height 2.75rem (44px) on both .action-btn and .act, focus-visible outlines on both.

summary: Source-review of the aria-actions family against w3c/aria PR #1805 (open/unmerged proposed text, not current normative ARIA), Chromium's exact implementation surface (aria_relationship_attributes.idl: [RuntimeEnabled=AriaActions] FrozenArray<Element>? ariaActionsElements — the reflection name is ariaActionsElements, not ariaActions; aria_properties.json5: IDREF_list, isGlobal with a 15-role prevented list; runtime feature AriaActions stable on Win/Mac/Linux only, not ChromeOS/Android per the M151 launch intent), and the direct chromestatus detail (updated 2026-07-01: desktop 151 'In development'; v151 listing Enabled by default). The family's core defect was asserting AT/a11y-tree exposure as demonstrated fact with no probe: both concepts now report author intent (content attribute), DOM-level reflection (live probe), and AT behavior (explicitly out of scope) as separate honest layers, with exact availability copy. Added focus-visible outlines, 44px tap targets, and complete keyboard/focus semantics for the tree pattern. Added the immutable root suite (9 assertions covering Element plus ElementInternals, the ariaActionsElements-vs-ariaActions name trap, and strict referenced-element resolution). Missing-suite denominator 9→8 expected (790/798).
